questions.q: What does the old joke 'the S in IoT stands for Security' imply?
options: IoT devices are often not secure
IoT always uses secure sockets
Security is the main selling point of IoT
IoT devices never connect to the internet
questions.explain: There is no 'S' in IoT — any internet-connected device needs security designed in.
questions.evidence: there is no 'S' in IoT, implying it is not secure

questions.q: A microcontroller's program memory is non-volatile. What does that mean?
options: It is erased every time the device restarts
It can only be written once in the factory
It is stored in the cloud rather than on the chip
What is written to it stays when the device has no power
questions.explain: Program memory keeps your code; data memory (RAM) is cleared when power is lost.
questions.evidence: Program memory is non-volatile, which means whatever is written to it stays when there is no power to the device.

questions.q: Which two functions make up the code of an Arduino sketch?
options: main and exit
start and stop
setup and loop
init and run
questions.explain: setup runs once when the board starts; loop then runs over and over.
questions.evidence: C/C++ code with 2 functions - setup and loop

questions.q: How are MQTT messages routed to clients?
options: Directly to each client's IP address
Through named topics, not directly to an individual client
By email to each subscriber
In arrival order through a message queue
questions.explain: Clients publish to and subscribe to topics on a broker, which forwards the messages.
questions.evidence: Messages are routed using named topics, rather than being sent directly to an individual client.

questions.q: With MQTT's 'at least once' delivery, what does the sender do?
options: Retries the message until an acknowledgement is received
Sends it once and never retries
Sends it to every topic at the same time
Holds it until the receiver asks for it
questions.explain: This acknowledged delivery can deliver a message more than once, but never loses it.
questions.evidence: the message is re-tried by the sender multiple times until acknowledgement is received

questions.q: Why are NoSQL databases also known as document databases?
options: They can only store PDF files
They need SQL documents to define their tables
They print reports as documents
They can store unstructured data such as documents
questions.explain: They lack the rigid table structure of SQL databases, so each record can have a different shape.
questions.evidence: They are also known as document databases as they can store unstructured data such as documents.
